items.stem: Which is a common and avoidable data-leakage surface in AI systems?

options.text: Logging full prompts and responses containing sensitive data
options.rationale: Correct: unredacted prompt/response logs are a frequent leak source.
Using a model is not itself a leak; how data is handled is.
Documentation is not a leakage surface.
Variable naming does not leak data.

items.explanation: Correct: unredacted prompt/response logs are a frequent leak source.

items.stem: Which TWO reduce the risk of secret leakage? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Store secrets in a vault and issue short-lived credentials
options.rationale: Correct: a vault with short-lived tokens limits exposure if one leaks.

options.text: Redact sensitive fields before they reach prompts and logs
options.rationale: Correct: redaction keeps sensitive data out of places it can leak.

options.text: Hard-code API keys directly in the prompt template
options.rationale: Secrets in prompts are easily exposed.

options.text: Email the production keys to the whole team
options.rationale: Broad distribution of secrets maximises leak risk.

items.explanation: Correct: a vault with short-lived tokens limits exposure if one leaks.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: What is the principle of least privilege applied to an AI component's data access?

options.text: Give each component access only to the data it genuinely needs
options.rationale: Correct: least privilege minimises what can leak from any one component.

options.text: Give every component full access for convenience
options.rationale: Broad access is the opposite of least privilege.

options.text: Remove all access so nothing works
options.rationale: Least privilege is minimal necessary access, not zero access.

options.text: Grant access based on seniority only
options.rationale: Access should follow need, not title.

items.explanation: Correct: least privilege minimises what can leak from any one component.
